Last updated: June 19, 2026
Ang Lee 李安
director
filmmaker

 

Ang Lee is a Taiwanese American film director born on October 23, 1954, in Pingtung, Taiwan. He studied theater at the National Taiwan University of Arts before emigrating to the United States, where he earned a B.F.A. in Theater from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and an M.F.A. in Film Production from New York University’s Tisch School of the Arts.

Lee spent several years in the early 1980s struggling to establish his filmmaking career, during which his wife supported the family while he wrote screenplays and cared for their children. His breakthrough came with the “Father Knows Best” trilogy — Pushing Hands (1992), The Wedding Banquet (1993), and Eat Drink Man Woman (1994) — intimate films exploring generational conflict and cultural identity within Taiwanese and Chinese American families.

He went on to direct across a remarkable range of genres and cultures, including Sense and Sensibility (1995), The Ice Storm (1997), Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon (2000), Brokeback Mountain (2005), and Life of Pi (2012). His willingness to move fluidly between Chinese-language and English-language filmmaking, and across wildly different subject matter, is widely regarded as singular in contemporary cinema.

Notable Accomplishments

1993: Golden Bear, Berlin International Film Festival for The Wedding Banquet

1996: Golden Bear, Berlin International Film Festival for Sense and Sensibility. The sole filmmaker to win twice.

2001: Golden Globe Best Foreign Language Film for Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon 

2006: Academy Award Best Director for Brokeback Mountain (2005), first non-white to win.

2006: Order of Brilliant Star with Grand Cordon, the second highest civilian award by the government of Taiwan.

2012: Knight of the French Ordre des Arts et des Lettres.

2013: Academy Award Best Director for Life of Pi (2012).

2020: BAFTA Fellowship for Outstanding Contributions to British Cinema.

2021: Knight of the French Legion of Honor.

2024: Japan's Praemium Imperiale.
